purpose: U4 allow-list of reviewed, accepted hand-rolled YAML/frontmatter readers. comms-format-lint check-b (OD-3) grandfathers a source file iff its repo-relative path appears here. Each entry is a bounded single-field scalar read, a structural test/rail assertion, or a surgical in-place rewrite where a full js-yaml round-trip would be wrong (bundle bloat, reformat, or lost formatting). New GENERAL YAML parsing must still use the shared js-yaml parser.

readers.reason: Bounded single-field read of run.yaml (`^status:\s*open`) — the run-date.ts bounded-legacy precedent the lint header blesses. A hook: adding js-yaml would bloat the hook bundle for one scalar check.

Surgical single-field frontmatter read + in-place rewrite of `recall_importance` (explicitly 'never a yaml.dump reformat'). A js-yaml load/dump round-trip would reserialize the whole doc and lose comments/ordering.
Bounded single-field read of `final_status` from a codex-review-trail frontmatter block, with whitespace/quote tolerance. Reads exactly one scalar; no general YAML structure is parsed.
Test — scans for the `surface_manifest:` section header to assert structural parity. Asserts on raw text shape by design, not a runtime reader.
Test — asserts frontmatter fence structure (`startsWith('---')`, split on the fence) on rendered skill output. Intentional structural assertion, not YAML parsing.
Rail — the declarative-surface rail intentionally scans the `surface_manifest:` block by regex to stay decoupled from js-yaml (the rail must not depend on the parser it may be validating).
Test — asserts frontmatter fence structure (`startsWith('---\nname: ')`) on registry-rendered skills. Intentional structural assertion, not YAML parsing.
